title: Staged migration runner and rollout-gate framework for Redwood Private upgrades
creator: Avery Chen
description: Deliver a resilient, auditable upgrade tooling suite for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) that combines staged rollouts, programmable gates, and a migration runner that safely executes stateful changes. This work covers: (1) a reusable migration runner daemon that executes idempotent schema and data migrations with transactional checkpoints and resumability; (2) a rollout-gates framework that integrates health probes, telemetry-based canaries, and policy-driven gating (e.g., latency, error rate, KV cache hit ratios); (3) LTS-aware compatibility checks so customers on long-term support channels can opt into compatible change sets; and (4) operator-facing tooling for dry-run, abort, and automatic rollback to last-known-good artifact. Target surface: Private control plane + on-prem conductor + CRDs that customers can operate in air-gapped environments. Emphasis on upgrade safety (no data loss), clear telemetry for post-upgrade verification, and minimal customer downtime.
acceptance_criteria: Migration runner can perform idempotent SQL and non-SQL migrations with explicit checkpoints and resume after interruption
Rollout gates support at least 3 signal types (latency, error-rate, custom probe) and can halt a rollout automatically
Compatibility checker flags incompatible changes against LTS channels and surfaces suggested mitigations
Tooling exposes dry-run output identical to a real run (including predicted downtime and affected services)
Operator APIs to abort or rollback an in-flight upgrade revert system to previous version and schema state within defined RTO (documentation defines target)
End-to-end test harness that runs on a reproducible on-prem topology (single-node and HA) and validates rollback scenarios
discussion: 2025-02-12 Avery Chen: Kickoff. Goal to bridge gaps between existing private upgrade conductor and migration docs. Focus on resumable migrations and programmable gates.

2025-02-18 Rafael Ortega: Initial design review. Decided to prefer transaction-chunked migrations with a WAL-style checkpoint file to support air-gapped resume. Concern: some customers use older Postgres versions; plan to provide shim steps.
2025-02-24 Product review (Maya Singh): Add policy templates for enterprise compliance teams (e.g., change freeze windows, manual-approval gate).
2025-02-27 Eng sync: Proof-of-concept runner completed for small migrations (DDL + backfill). Need to harden idempotency guarantees and add schema-version pinned artifacts for LTS channels.
2025-02-28 Security (Jules Park): KMS integration required for migrations that handle encrypted payloads. Added security_review_required flag.
2025-03-01 Rafael Ortega: Implemented basic gate engine prototype (HTTP probe + Prometheus query). Next: integrate with Console rollout UI and test canary thresholds.
implementation_notes: Runner will be implemented as a lightweight k8s Job + sidecar controller for on-prem conductor; also provide a binary for air-gapped customers that mounts checkpoint files to a shared PVC
Migrations authored as a sequence of idempotent steps (RFC: include an idempotency token and guard queries). Support SQL and Go-based data transforms.
Gates modeled as composable predicates evaluated against Prometheus/HTTP/Custom metrics with backoff and retry semantics; policy DSL to be TLA: rgates v1
Compatibility checker reads component manifests and validates API stability against LTS compatibility matrix maintained in repo
Rollbacks will rely on maintaining previous artifact images and a reversible migration path where possible; when not possible, provide automated compensation jobs and operator prompts
Telemetry: annotate rollout timeline with migration checkpoints, probe snapshots, and decision logs for compliance/audit
testing_plan: Create an automated test matrix: (a) single-node installer upgrade, (b) HA cluster upgrade with live traffic generator, (c) interrupted migration resume tests, (d) canary halt and rollback, (e) LTS compatibility gating. Tests run in CI for quick iterations and in a dedicated on-prem lab for full end-to-end validation. Include chaos injections (network partition, node reboots) and measure RPO/RTO metrics.
